newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end flat, upside seen limited.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end flat, upside seen limited.

text.p: Austrian shares ended a shade in positive territory on Monday after see-saw trade and traders expect the market to show few gyrations over the short term.
"The market's a bit rudderless at the moment....I wouldn't be surprised if we closed out the week at these levels," said one trader, adding that underlying sentiment is firm.
The ATX added on just 1.95 points, or 0.16 percent, to end at 1,245.96 with 14 shares advancing, six falling and one unchanged by the close.
Investor activity was subdued and the blue-chip ATX index is seen capped at around 1,250 points in the absence of fresh trading incentives.
"It doesn't look like we're about to go above 1,250, unless there's a sudden influx of very big buy orders -- which don't seem in evidence at the moment," said another trader.
"There's hardly any demand at current levels," he added.
The day's best performer was cartonboard manufacturer Mayr-Melnhof, up 2.94 percent at 630, while the leading decliner was fireproof materials maker Radex, shedding 2.05 percent to 429 schillings.
The all-share Vienna bourse index gained 1.06 points, or 0.23 percent, to 462.28.
The March ATX future lost 0.4 points to 1,246.6 on turnover of 379 contracts. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 256
